The problem

Field survey data can contain impossible values, missing identifiers, statistical drift, and unusual response patterns. Supervisors need defensible evidence to prioritize investigation.

Who it is for

Survey supervisors and administrators investigating data quality in a hackathon/demo workflow.

Engineering challenge

Avoid treating unusual records as invalid. Hard-rule violations and statistical/ML review flags have distinct classifications; deterministic fallbacks keep the workflow usable without AI.

Architecture

  1. CSV / eSIGMA JSON → canonical schema → Parquet
  2. SIRL profiling → rules + statistics + Isolation Forest
  3. Evidence fusion → classification → optional explanation
  4. Supervisor dashboard → investigation + audit trail

Simplified architecture based on repository documentation.

Technology choices

  • FastAPI
  • Next.js
  • SQLite
  • Pandas
  • Isolation Forest

The stack above is documented in the repository. The architecture separates interface, execution or business logic, and persistence.

Documented implementation

  • Deterministic profiling and multi-channel validation
  • Risk scoring with confirmed/review/normal classification
  • Record evidence drill-down and hierarchical analytics
  • Investigation workflow, audit trail, CSV and Excel export

Current limits

Synthetic/demo extracts, hackathon-scale SQLite and Parquet, and no production eSIGMA authentication/VPN acceptance. Core validation APIs are intentionally unauthenticated in this build; demo login is not production RBAC.

Design takeaway

Explainability is part of the architecture: an explanation layer should not acquire authority over the underlying evidence.

This is an architectural interpretation of the documented implementation, not a measured outcome or a personal claim.
